demos.title: Water
demos.summary: This is liquid water, magnified a hundred million times. Each V is one molecule, an oxygen holding two hydrogens, tumbling and tugging at its neighbours. Reach in and pull one out.
demos.hint: Pinch a molecule and pull it out of the water.

demos.title: A crystal full of corridors
demos.summary: Cool atoms down and they lock into a repeating pattern. This zeolite, a crystal of silicon and oxygen, is threaded with corridors barely wider than a molecule. Make it big and look down one.
demos.hint: Pinch with both hands and spread them to step inside.
demos.observation: Find the repeating channels through the ZSM-5 framework. Empty space is part of the structure.
demos.interactionNote: Start in Observe, then step inside. Hands perturb the model; reset to return to the original crystal.

demos.title: Restless atoms
demos.summary: Even in a solid, atoms on the surface never sit still. The bright atoms are loose nickel atoms on a nickel crystal, hopping from one hollow to the next. Watch them wander, meet and cling together.
demos.hint: Pinch a bright atom and drop it somewhere else on the surface.

demos.title: A nanoparticle grows
demos.summary: A speck of silicon carbide, a few nanometres across, floats among a few dozen loose carbon atoms. As it cools from 2200 K, they stick to it and the particle grows. Keep an eye on the temperature.
demos.hint: Watch the temperature fall as loose atoms stick to the particle.

demos.title: Breaking point
demos.summary: Roll a sheet of carbon into a tube and you get one of the strongest materials known. Here its two ends are pulled apart, slowly. Watch the hexagons stretch, then snap where atoms are missing.
demos.hint: Pinch an atom to tug on the tube yourself.

demos.title: A ring of carbon
demos.summary: Twelve atoms. A familiar shape. Meet benzene at the scale of your hands.
demos.observation: Find the six-carbon ring, then gently pull one atom. The bond network responds to the empirical potential.
demos.interactionNote: Open your hand, pinch near an atom, then move slowly. Strong pulls can change this carbon–hydrogen model.

demos.title: Four directions
demos.summary: One carbon, four hydrogens. Discover the tetrahedral shape hidden inside methane.
demos.observation: Turn the molecule and find the four directions around carbon. Compare this three-dimensional shape with the flat benzene ring.
demos.interactionNote: Pinch the carbon with one hand and a hydrogen with the other. Move gently to feel the molecular geometry respond.

demos.title: A little room to turn
demos.summary: Two carbons, six hydrogens. Explore how a small molecule can twist in three dimensions.
demos.observation: Look down the carbon–carbon axis. Follow the staggered arrangement of the hydrogen atoms.
demos.interactionNote: Hold one carbon and gently move the other. Stronger pulls drive this empirical model; bond changes are not guaranteed.

demos.title: Carbon workshop
demos.summary: Bend a sheet one atom thick. Discover how a carbon network shares the strain.
demos.observation: Pull at an edge, release, and watch the sheet respond. Bond changes depend on how the atoms meet.
demos.interactionNote: Pinch two atoms to stretch the network. Rejoining broken edges is an experiment, not a guaranteed reaction.

demos.title: Carbon, in another form
demos.summary: The same element, a different world. Explore a tiny diamond lattice in three dimensions.
demos.observation: Compare this three-dimensional network with the flexible carbon sheet. Look for the tetrahedral geometry.
demos.interactionNote: Push a surface atom and watch its neighbours respond. Step inside to inspect the network.

demos.title: Water vapor
demos.summary: Follow one water molecule as it tumbles through a sparse cloud. A familiar substance, seen differently.
demos.observation: Follow one oxygen and its two hydrogen neighbours through a dilute gas.
demos.interactionNote: This is the bundled empirical water model. It is not a general-purpose reaction experiment.

demos.title: Peptide in water
demos.summary: Dynamics of a small solvated peptide chain (5-mer).
demos.previewNote: 84 peptide atoms shown · live solvent omitted from preview
demos.observation: Trace the five-residue peptide among its surrounding water.
demos.interactionNote: Fixed molecular topology; observe fluctuations rather than chemical reactions.

demos.title: Graphene oxide nanoparticle
demos.summary: A graphene oxide particle with a few water molecules around it.

demos.title: RDX explosive
demos.summary: RDX, an explosive, simulated with the reactive ReaxFF force field.

demos.title: Silica beta cristobalite
demos.summary: Beta cristobalite silica crystal with the Vashishta potential.

demos.title: Large nanoporous zeolite (23,040 atoms)
demos.summary: A bigger ZSM-5 crystal, 4 by 4 by 5 unit cells, with its channels running all the way through. Use billboards to see every atom.

demos.title: Nanoporous silica glass
demos.summary: Amorphous silica with 75% porosity from the Atomify web app: 192,000 simulated atoms drawn as 3 by 3 by 3 periodic copies, 5.2 million atoms and 68 nm across. Use Step inside to fly through the pores.

demos.title: Shear in nickel
demos.summary: Sideways shear applied to a nickel slab, with the embedded atom method.

demos.title: Lennard-Jones fluid
demos.summary: A binary Lennard-Jones gas of small and large particles.

demos.title: Large liquid (108,000 atoms)
demos.summary: A Lennard-Jones liquid big enough to need billboards, which it switches to when it opens.

demos.title: Diffusion (10,000 particles)
demos.summary: About 10,000 Lennard-Jones particles with masses 1 and 4, starting as a slab of light ones. The heavy ones diffuse half as fast.

demos.title: Pouring grains
demos.summary: Pouring of granular particles into a 3d box, then chute flow.

demos.title: Depositing molecules
demos.summary: Deposition of molecules onto a 3d substrate.

demos.title: Crack 2D
demos.summary: Crack propagation in a 2d solid.

demos.title: Friction 2D
demos.summary: Frictional contact of spherical asperities between 2d surfaces.

demos.title: Tiny chains, gathering
demos.summary: Water-loving heads and water-avoiding tails organise in a two-dimensional model.
demos.previewNote: 2D surfactant model · one bead represents a coarse-grained part
demos.observation: Follow water-loving heads and water-avoiding tails as groups organise.
demos.interactionNote: A two-dimensional model, not a complete membrane.

demos.title: Flow past an obstacle
demos.summary: Flow around two voids in a 2d channel.

demos.title: The threads of life
demos.summary: A 20-base-pair DNA duplex. Follow two complementary strands and watch the helix breathe.
demos.observation: A 20-base-pair DNA duplex. Follow two complementary strands and watch the helix breathe.
demos.interactionNote: Observe this model and inspect its particles using the controls.

demos.title: When a solid lets go
demos.summary: Follow an ordered model crystal as heating lets its particles rearrange.
demos.observation: Follow an ordered model crystal as heating lets its particles rearrange.
demos.interactionNote: Observe this model and inspect its particles using the controls.

demos.title: A seed becomes a crystal
demos.summary: Cool a liquid around a small fixed seed and watch local order grow.
demos.observation: Cool a liquid around a small fixed seed and watch local order grow.
demos.interactionNote: Observe this model and inspect its particles using the controls.

demos.title: Ice becomes water
demos.summary: Watch a 512-molecule ice network lose its order as whole water molecules become mobile.
demos.previewNote: mW water · each sphere is a whole H₂O molecule
demos.observation: Watch a 512-molecule ice network lose its order as whole water molecules become mobile.

demos.title: Where reaction heat comes from
demos.summary: Ignite a tiny methane–oxygen reactor. Follow real products and the exchange between potential and kinetic energy.
